title: Applied ML Eval Harness & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standards and operational procedures for the applied-ML evaluation stack: the eval harness, prompt sets & benchmarks, model onboarding flows, automated quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and the regression triage process. It is intended for ML engineers, applied-ML reviewers, and SREs who operate model evaluation, release gating, and regression response.

Purpose and Scope:
- Provide a single reference for how models are evaluated end-to-end prior to and during serving rollouts.
- Define ownership, SLOs, tooling, and runbooks for detecting and remediating quality regressions.
- Cover both automated gating (CI) and operational processes (oncall triage, rollout rollback).
- Applicable to all model classes used in Redwood: chat/generation, completion, embeddings, and reranking.

Owners and Roles:
- Eval Harness Owner: Applied ML team (primary contact: Asha Patel).
- Model Onboarding Owner: Model Infrastructure (liaison: Diego Ramirez).
- Regression Triage Lead: Reliability / Applied ML (Priya Nair).
- Oncall: Eng-SRE (first responder), Applied-ML (subject-matter).
- Reviewers: Applied-ML, Product QA, Customer Success for customer-facing models.

High-level Architecture (eval harness):
- CI integration: eval-harness runs as a GitHub Actions job (workflow: .github/workflows/eval-harness.yml) and as a periodic batch job in Airflow (dag: eval_harness_daily).
- Data sources: canonical prompt-sets (S3: s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/), curated holdouts, and synthetic scenario generators.
- Metrics backend: Prometheus (for infra metrics) + BigQuery for evaluation results and signal comparisons.
- Alerts / Dashboards: Grafana dashboards per-model and per-route; Slack channel #eval-alerts for triage.

Prompt Sets & Benchmarks (standards):
- Prompt set format: JSONL with fields: id, scenario, input, expected_output_metadata, tags, difficulty. Example snippet in content below.
- Benchmarks: Each prompt set must include an explicit acceptance criterion (e.g., pass rate >= 92% on safety checks, BLEU >= X for task Y, embedding cosine recall >= 0.87).
- Ownership: prompt sets are versioned in repo redwood/eval-prompt-sets. Changes require a PR with: description, labels (motivation/regression/corpus-change), reviewer from applied-ml.

Model Onboarding Guide (minimum required steps):
1. Pre-onboarding checklist:
   - Define model intent & primary workloads (chat/completion/embeddings).
   - Provide model artifact location and reproducible build (container or weights + tokenizer).
   - Provide unit evals, prompt sets, and a release note describing expected strengths/weaknesses.
2. Local compatibility tests:
   - Tokenization parity (compare token counts vs reference).
   - KV cache correctness tests for transformer decoders.
3. Eval harness integration:
   - Add model to eval catalog (file: models/catalog.yaml), set model tags and quantization compatibility.
   - Configure CI job: .github/workflows/eval-<model>.yml that runs the core prompt sets and collects metrics to BigQuery.
4. Canary rollout gating criteria (must pass before canary):
   - Functional pass rate >= baseline - 1.5% (or agreed delta).
   - Latency P95 <= target latency for the model family (see Performance SLOs table).
   - Reranking/embedding recall: within 2% of baseline for top-k retrieval tests.
5. Post-canary checks and promotion: automated quality checks and human review sign-off.

Quality Guardrails (automated & human-in-the-loop):
- Automated checks (run on every PR and nightly):
  - Safety classifiers (toxicity/safety filters) must not degrade beyond 0.5% absolute on safety-sensitive prompt sets.
  - Distributional checks: embedding drift, perplexity shift, tokenization divergence.
  - Regression detectors: change point detection on pass/fail rates; raise alert if p < 0.01.
- Human review triggers:
  - If automated safety check fails for >= 3 prompts in a set flagged as critical.
  - For changes to prompt set composition or addition of synthetic adversarial cases.

Quantization Profiles (guidelines):
- Profile naming: <model>-<arch>-<quant>-<profile-version> (e.g., vicuna-13b-4bit-q4f16-v1).
- Supported profiles: fp16, int8, q4f16, q5_K_mixed.
- Recommended steps:
  1. Start with fp16 baseline and run the full eval suite.
  2. Run q4f16 profile, measure quality delta; accept if within spec (e.g., task-specific metric delta <= 1.5%).
  3. If int8 enabled, run targeted stress tests for numeric stability (long-context continuations, arithmetic tasks).
- Example quantization config (JSONL string in repo):
  {
    "profile_name": "vicuna-13b-q4f16-v2",
    "quant_backend": "fbgemm",
    "block_size": "64",
    "calibration_examples": "s3://redwood-calib/vicuna-13b/calib-5000.jsonl"
  }

Regression Triage Playbook (operational runbook):
- Detection:
  1. Alert fires from eval-harness CI, nightly batch, or production monitoring (alert channels: #eval-alerts, PagerDuty: PD_ID EVAL_REGRESSION).
  2. First-responder (Eng-SRE) acknowledges and posts initial summary in Slack with tags: model, commit, eval-suite, delta metrics.
- Triage Steps (first 30 minutes):
  1. Validate the alert: re-run the failing eval locally via the eval-harness runner with the identified commit.
     - CLI: python -m eval_harness.run --model <model> --suite <suite> --commit <sha> --output debug.json
  2. Identify scope: is the regression across all prompt sets, a single benchmark, or specific tag (safety/perf)?
  3. Rollback/mitigate: If production impact is confirmed or regression is severe (pass rate drop > 3% on customer-facing suite), trigger immediate rollback to previous model version and notify Customer Success.
- Deeper analysis (first 8 hours):
  1. Build a regression report: compare metrics across commits, run ablation tests (quantization on/off, tokenization diff, prompt-engineering variants).
  2. Assign an owner from applied-ml and open a regression issue (labels: regression, priority=P1/P2).
  3. If root cause is model change, create a targeted fix or reweight prompt sets; if infra-related, involve Model Infra/SRE.
- Postmortem and Preventative Actions (within 7 days):
  - Produce a 72-hour RCA document with action items, owners, and ETA.
  - Add or update automated checks to catch similar regressions in CI.

Metrics, Thresholds and SLOs (representative):
- Functional pass rate (per prompt-set): target >= 94% for customer-facing models. Alert at delta >= 1.5% from baseline.
- Safety pass rate: no absolute drop > 0.5% allowed without manual approval.
- Latency SLOs: P95 <= 350ms for small models, P95 <= 900ms for 13B-class models (on dedicated infra).
- Embedding recall@10: baseline - 2% threshold for alert.

CI/CD Integration and Gating:
- Required gates before merge to main for model or prompt-set changes:
  1. Unit tests + style checks.
  2. Eval harness CI: run core prompt-sets and safety checks (must pass).
  3. Nightly full-suite run must succeed (for model changes) before scheduled promotion to canary.
- Pull Request checklist (example):
  - [ ] Model artifact uploaded and checksum verified.
  - [ ] Eval results attached (BigQuery link).
  - [ ] Reviewer from applied-ml assigned.
  - [ ] Quantization profile (if used) included and validated.

Example prompt-set JSONL snippet (schema):
{"id":"ps-2028-001","scenario":"email-summarization","input":"<long email body>","expected_output_metadata":"length<=50;contains_summary=true","tags":["summarization","customer-support"],"difficulty":"medium"}

Example eval-harness run (CLI):
- Quick local run: python -m eval_harness.run --model vicuna-13b --suite customer-support --limit 200
- Full nightly: airflow trigger_dag eval_harness_daily --conf '{"models":["vicuna-13b","mpt-30b"]}'

Dashboards and Reporting:
- Must have per-model dashboards in Grafana: 
  - eval_overview: pass-rate, safety-pass, avg-rouge/bleu, embedding-recall@k
  - latency_and_cost: token-CPU/GPU time breakdown, memory trends, quantization impact.
- Weekly QA digest: scheduled BigQuery job generates a PDF report and posts to #eval-weekly with highlights and anomalies.

Change Management and Documentation Policy:
- All prompt-set or eval-suite changes require a changelog entry and a migration plan if they alter acceptance criteria.
- Major model upgrades (architecture or training data changes) must be coordinated with Product and Customer Success; notify customers on Dedicated/Private at least 2 weeks prior.

Appendix A — Example Regression Report Template (fields):
- Title, Date, Model, Commit SHA, Triggering Metric, Delta vs Baseline, Affected Prompt Sets, Repro Steps, Temporary Mitigation, Owner, RCA, Action Items.

Appendix B — Quick Links:
- Eval prompt sets repo: https://git.redwood.internal/redwood/eval-prompt-sets
- Eval harness runner: https://git.redwood.internal/redwood/eval-harness
- BigQuery dataset: redwood_evals.results
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/eval-dashboards

- When to update: after any change to CI, prompt-sets, or quantization defaults.
